key_insight: Explicitly modeling inter-object occlusions within a 3D layout-conditioned generator produces depth-consistent, correctly scaled partially-occluded objects, improving realism where existing methods fail.
problem_solved: Prior 3D layout-conditioned text-to-image methods often ignore precise occlusion reasoning, producing incorrect depth/overlap and scale when objects partially occlude each other; this work addresses that gap by making occlusion an explicit part of the scene representation and generation pipeline.
method: Introduce an occlusion-aware 3D scene representation that encodes per-object depth and visibility (occlusion masks) alongside layout conditioning.
Integrate occlusion information into the generative model (e.g., layout-conditioned diffusion) with differentiable compositing so occluded geometry and appearance are synthesized consistently.
Train with losses and supervision that enforce depth consistency, correct occlusion ordering, and visual fidelity (using rendered occluded examples or self-supervision).
impact: Improves realism and controllability of multi-object scene synthesis, enabling reliable partial-occlusion rendering for content creation, AR/VR, and simulation; reduces manual post-editing and enables physically plausible layouts.
visual_elements: Before/After image triplet: input layout, generation without occlusion reasoning, generation with SeeThrough3D (highlight corrected overlaps)
Pipeline diagram: occlusion-aware 3D representation → occlusion mask/depth module → differentiable compositing → layout-conditioned generator
Overlay visualizations: predicted depth maps and per-object occlusion masks over generated images
Bar/chart: quantitative metrics (occlusion accuracy, depth error, FID) comparing baseline vs SeeThrough3D
paper_title: SeeThrough3D: Occlusion Aware 3D Control in Text-to-Image Generation
paper_authors: Vaibhav Agrawal, Rishubh Parihar, Pradhaan Bhat, Ravi Kiran Sarvadevabhatla, R. Venkatesh Babu
